claim: CLS-06's third REQUEST_INFO branch (the driver canceled and the record gives no reason) is missing from the DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition and from PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1. Both send that case to CW-OTHER, while CLS-06 and the engine give REQUEST_INFO. The round 2 brief's claim that 'the rule, the DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition, PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 and the engine now agree' (CONS-1) therefore does not hold on this branch.
how: The DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition and PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 name every CLS-06 branch: a driver cancellation with no reason, records that disagree or cannot be read, or silent records give REQUEST_INFO at tier HUMAN; a system cancellation goes to CW-OTHER.

claim: itinerary_change, added in round 1 (ADV-2, F4), reads ordinary records as an accepted itinerary change. The fee-line regex 'destination|stop|edit' matches inside 'credit', so any credit line counts as a destination-change fee. The system-message test fires on booking or completion messages that contain 'destination' or 'drop-off' plus 'confirmed'. In run() this turns an FC-TOLL detour refund (APPROVE) into ESCALATE_HUMAN (HUMAN). In fc_r01 it marks a fixed fare as RECALCULATED, so FC-R01 does not apply, no FC-TOLL claim opens and nothing escalates. Separately, a request explicitly declined (details 'Driver declined', even with destination_edit_accepted: False) still returns None and escalates, against Ryde's 'If the driver rejects, the previous trip details remain.' No test covers these negative cases or the `charged > 0` clause.
how: itinerary_change is rewritten: fee keys are matched as whole tokens and credit, discount, promo, refund, voucher, card and bus keys are excluded; a system message or event counts only when it is about a change of destination, drop-off or stop; a declined request is no change. Tests T47 and T48.

claim: The engine does not follow CLS-06 for a system cancellation with no reason. CLS-06, the DT precondition and the PB step all say the system canceled -> CW-OTHER, but the engine requires a reason for SYSTEM as well as for DRIVER. It returns REQUEST_INFO, and its trace says 'the driver canceled', which is false.
how: A system cancellation goes to CW-OTHER whether or not a reason is recorded, and the trace names the system (V116).

claim: The CONS-16 fix exempts a double-quoted span when it is any substring of any clause quote, so a bare quoted number is exempt. EXP-03's new text exempts only 'Numbers inside a verbatim quote of a clause'.
how: The quote exemption needs at least three words and a verbatim clause quote; a bare quoted number is checked (a4_check).

claim: The CONS-3/ADV-7 fix says the stand-in now matches whole words so ordinary no-show chat does not fire it. The v0.1 stems kept as prefixes still fire on common no-show text: '\baccident' on 'accidentally' and '\bcrash' on 'the app crashed'. D40 (a) records only misses, not false hits.
how: SAFETY_IGNORE removes 'accidentally', 'by accident' and app or phone crashes first; 'accident' and 'crash' are whole words. a4_check pins the texts.

claim: Round 1 F7's second part was not addressed. CLS-01's 'or any other crime' still has no boundary with fraud or overcharging, and the fix now cites Code of Conduct item 6, whose text lists 'acts of vandalism or damage to property'. With 'When it is unclear whether text is safety content, it is treated as safety content (S1)', an applier can read a damage or overcharge complaint as safety content. The FC-DRIVERCHARGE excludes imply the opposite only for made-up charges.
how: CLS-01 says a dispute about money or damage to the car is not safety content by itself, even where the conduct may be a crime; it becomes safety content with violence, threats, danger, abuse or discrimination.

claim: The records of what is left for Jasper are incomplete. NEXT_STEPS's 'To decide (A4, open item D40 (a) to (j))' line summarizes only (a) to (e). The judgments added in round 1 are not mentioned: (f) the narrowed 'stranded' and the removal of a rider under the influence, (h) the FC-R12 materiality that keeps RydeSEND automatic, (i) and (j). D40's changed text says only 'records that disagree or are silent give REQUEST_INFO' and omits the driver-without-reason branch. It also does not say that FX9's EXP-01 labels and FC-R01 toll caveat were done before A4, so FX9 reads as four of six items done, which matters for A5's CHANGELOG (every rule with its FX). Line 29 still says FX8 and FX9 'can go into A4 or A5'.
how: NEXT_STEPS's line covers D40 (a) to (l).

claim: The A4 census patch (census_a4.py) left two census notes stale after A4's changes.
how: census_a4.py updates the CW-F02B and CW-R08 notes.

claim: SG-9 was fixed only on the stop_added event row. The has_dropoff relation note and D40 still say the drop-off list changes at stop_added, which contradicts the fixed row ('none until the driver accepts'). CLS-06 also reads a cancelled_by field that the ontology's data contract (ENT-TRIP attributes) does not define.
how: The dropoffs attribute, the has_dropoff relation and D40 say the list changes when the driver accepts; ENT-TRIP has an optional cancelled_by attribute.

claim: CLS-06 applies to CW-RIDERCANCEL (an adjudicated, in-scope type), but PB-CW-RIDERCANCEL has no CLS-06 precondition step. PB-CW-NOSHOW does. A rider-cancel playbook run therefore never checks that the records agree the rider canceled. CLS-05 also still says only CLS-02 handles contradictions with the organizer code and does not mention that CLS-06's trip record takes precedence.
how: PB-CW-RIDERCANCEL step 1 checks CLS-06 first; CLS-05 says the trip record decides a cancellation-fee type over the code.

claim: Two census rows that A4 made stale were not updated. (1) The CW-R08 'not moving' row still says a source for that ground would make the rule C again. This is false since A4, because the advance-booking ETA is also a counted D element. SG-2 fixed the same sentence in the rule's credibility_note and in D39 (e), but not here. The row also does not mention the new qualifier that a driver already waiting counts as moving. (2) The CW-F02B conflict row still lists the 2024 driver pages as an FX9 leftover 'not done' that 'could be added', although A4 added RYDE-20244064619161 (and names RYDE-33362932998937) to CW-F02B.
how: As R2-FID-8; the CW-R08 element names both qualifiers.

claim: The new CLS-01 census row (A) lists examples whose quotes are not in its source column, and it counts as Ryde's an element that the rule labels FairRyde's. The element names 'reckless driving' (Code item 7) and 'alcohol and drugs' (item 8), but the source column cites only items 5 and 6 and the community standards. It also counts 'similar grounds' as A, while CLS-01's FAIRRYDE note lists 'religion and similar grounds read into Ryde's etc' as FairRyde's (D).
how: The CLS-01 row quotes Code of Conduct items 7 and 8 and uses Ryde's words for the discrimination grounds; religion stays in the FAIRRYDE row.

claim: FC-F01's added-stop element is not fully supported by its quotes, and its credibility reasoning is inconsistent. (1) Neither new quote says the fare is recalculated after an added stop. The note on RYDE-51399674412441 claims 'the same edit request and fare confirmation', but the fare confirmation is step 7 of that article, which is not quoted. (2) The credibility_note rates the added-stop part B because of the driver article's pilot status, but keeps the changed-drop-off part at A. The same driver article's pilot caveat covers both ('change the drop-off and/or add an additional drop-off stop ... *This feature is currently in a pilot phase'). Under credibility_scale A ('not contradicted by another Ryde page'), both parts should then be B.
how: FC-F01 cites the rider article's next step 'New destination and fare confirmation will be displayed.'; the note no longer claims more than the quotes.

claim: The round 1 fix for F7 is incomplete. F7 also said that 'or any other crime' has no stated boundary with fraud and overcharging, and the fix only added the item 6 quote. Ryde's community standards call overcharging 'Fraudulent Activity' that may lead to 'legal prosecution, which may result in possible imprisonment'. CLS-01 counts 'any other crime' and treats unclear text as safety content. SE-CONDUCT is now anchored on conduct 'that Ryde lists as misconduct between drivers and passengers (... community standards)', and those standards call overcharging misconduct. Neither CLS-01, FC-ROUTE nor FC-TOLL says that an allegation of overcharging or cheating on the fare is not, by itself, safety content. Only FC-DRIVERCHARGE's excludes implies it.
how: As R2-FID-6.

claim: The DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition and PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 leave out CLS-06's third REQUEST_INFO case (the driver canceled and the record gives no reason). Their wording sends that case to CW-OTHER as 'another driver cancellation', while CLS-06 and the engine give REQUEST_INFO. CONS-1's disposition says the four now give the same outcomes.
how: The DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition and PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 name every CLS-06 branch: a driver cancellation with no reason, records that disagree or cannot be read, or silent records give REQUEST_INFO at tier HUMAN; a system cancellation goes to CW-OTHER.

claim: FC-FAREMISMATCH lists what can legitimately explain a charged fare above the quote (an accepted destination change, ERP, a listed surcharge, a tip) but leaves out the waiting time fee. Ryde adds that fee to the fare at the end of the trip, and Ryde's surcharge list does not include it. Its excludes also do not point to CW-WAITING.
how: FC-FAREMISMATCH names the waiting time fee in its definition and excludes (CW-WAITING).

claim: The rewritten FC-F02 zh still leaves out parts of the English: the definition of the extra distance ('extra distance = actual minus recommended'), the corridor width ('beyond CORRIDOR_HALF_WIDTH_M') and 'ignoring ENDPOINT_EXCLUSION_M at both ends'. The omission predates A4, but A4 rewrote this zh and carried it over.
how: FC-F02's zh is complete (extra distance, corridor width, endpoint exclusion).

claim: The recommended_route note, rewritten for SG-8 and CONS-10, says FC-R12 applies whenever a route after an itinerary change is not marked final_itinerary. Since the F2 fix, FC-R12 applies to a changed itinerary only when the recommended route can change the amount.
how: The recommended_route note states FC-R12's materiality condition.

claim: itinerary_change (the round 1 fix for ADV-2) still misses changed itineraries recorded with ordinary wording. When it misses one, run() compares the ERP against the stale recommended route and upholds automatically, although FC-R12 requires escalation. Five gaps: (1) a negation word anywhere in a system message cancels the message; (2) a system message that only reports a request returns False, not None; (3) a system message without one of five verbs is not read; (4) event names other than the three exact codes are not read, and neither are their details; (5) fee-line keys such as 'dropoff_change_fee' and amounts such as '$3.00' are not read. ADV-2 named 'other event spellings' and 'a system chat message', and its disposition says fixed.
how: itinerary_change reads events of any spelling (normalized type plus details), system messages by sentence with negation only in the accepting sentence, a request alone as a possible change, and fee lines with currency text. Tests T49 to T52.

claim: canceling_party (the round 1 fix for F1, ADV-1 and CONS-1) treats any record it cannot parse as silent and drops it. When such a record names the rider or the system, the remaining reason (rider_no_show, read as DRIVER) decides alone, and the fee is upheld automatically. Records it drops: a cancelled_by value outside five exact strings; an event spelled 'rider_canceled' or 'trip_cancelled' (details are not read); a system message saying 'customer', 'You cancelled' or 'auto-cancelled'; a system row typed 'System'. CLS-06 and PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 ('according to every record in the trip record') and the DT precondition ('all agree') require REQUEST_INFO when a record says otherwise.
how: canceling_party maps any cancelled_by by content (rider, passenger, customer, user; driver; system, platform, auto, admin) and treats a value it cannot read as disagreeing; it reads any cancel event (normalized spelling, details when the type names no party), system messages with customer, 'you cancelled' and auto-cancel wording, and chat types in any case. Tests V113 to V115.

claim: Round 1 widened CLS-01 to abuse or harassment of any kind (ADV-6, D40 (e)). The safety stand-in did not follow. It catches only 'insulted me', 'slur' and 'commented on my looks/body/appearance'. CLS-01's own new examples are not caught: swearing at someone, name-calling, contacting a passenger after the trip, advances in chat, intimidation without the word 'threat', and discrimination without 'racist' or 'discriminat'. These are the safety texts most likely in a no-show dispute (a call or chat with the driver), and the engine upholds the fee automatically. D40 (a) discloses that paraphrases are missed, but these are CLS-01's literal examples, and none of the a4_check pins tests them.
how: Patterns added for swearing at someone, name-calling, personal questions, asking whether the rider lives alone, and contact after the trip; the stand-in still misses paraphrases (D40 (a)).

claim: The round 1 fix for ADV-13 is incomplete. ADV-13's own failure scenario was 'the driver parked 300 m away at 17:50 waiting' for an 18:00 advance booking. The fix exempts only 'a driver already waiting at the pick-up', so that scenario still makes the fee waivable ('not moving toward the pick-up point'). Round 1's skeptic rated ADV-13 MINOR because 'CW-R08 is D and the waiver needs approval'. By D39 (h), a D outcome rule is decisive only through a decision-table row. CW-RIDERCANCEL has no table, CW-R08 is HARD, and the 'not moving' ground has no parameter. So the waiver can be automatic.
how: CW-R08: for an advance booking a driver who is not moving is a ground only when the driver could no longer arrive by the assignment ETA plus the grace. Whether every CW-R08 waiver should need approval is recorded for Jasper, D40 (k).

claim: Round 1 rewrote the stand-in as whole-word patterns. The rewrite dropped catches the A4 draft list had for CLS-01's unsafe drop-off and being-held examples. The 'made' alternative in `(told|asked|made|forced|ordered) me to get out` can never match natural English ('made me get out' has no 'to'). 'locked the door(s)', 'driving dangerously', 'dropped me in the middle of the expressway' and 'punched the dashboard' no longer fire. These are mostly trip events, so in the no-show scope the tier effect is rare.
how: Patterns for 'made me get out', 'he locked the doors', 'would not stop when asked', 'driving dangerously', 'dropped me in the middle of the expressway' and being left at night; a4_check pins them.

claim: Safe-direction false positives that are frequent in fee disputes remain after round 1's whole-word rewrite (CONS-3, ADV-7). The prefix patterns \baccident, \bcrash, \bthreat, \bpolice\b, \babus..., \binjur and \bfight fire on 'accidentally', 'my app crashed', 'threatened to cancel', 'I will make a police report', 'abuse of the no-show fee' and 'my kid was injured'. Such a routine case goes to tier HUMAN (gate G4), and both parties are told 'The case includes a safety concern'. The words predate A4 (v0.1), but round 1 claimed whole-word matching.
how: As R2-FID-5; 'threatened to cancel' and 'fight this charge' are removed first; 'unsafe' needs a person feeling unsafe or an unsafe drop-off, place or driving.

claim: itinerary_change also has false positives that send ERP claims to a person, and in fc_r01 they turn a fixed fare into RECALCULATED. The fee-key test matches 'edit' inside 'credit'. The system-message test is bag-of-words: any of destination, drop-off or stop plus any of confirmed, accepted, updated, changed or added. A request followed by a rejection is still None. For fc_r01, a misread change means FC-R01 does not apply, the auto-opened FC-TOLL claim (R1's S$4.00) disappears, and nothing escalates.
how: As R2-FID-2.

claim: The EXP-03 quote exemption (the round 1 fix for CONS-16) exempts any double-quoted span that is a substring of any clause quote in the KB, not only a verbatim clause quote. Bare quoted numbers and amounts such as "7", "$5.00", "8 min" and "2026" are therefore exempt, so an explanation can state an unregistered number by putting it in quotes.
how: As R2-FID-4.

claim: FC-R12's text defines ERP materiality as 'ERP was charged and the actual path passed an active gantry'. The engine and D40 (h) use the rider's share of the actual ERP being above 0. They disagree for RydeSEND (share 0) and for active gantries at a zero rate. An LLM applying FC-R12 escalates a RydeSEND claim with ERP charged and a changed itinerary. The engine refunds it under FC-R07 at APPROVE. D40 (h)'s 'a RydeSEND claim ... keeps its automatic ruling' holds only when no ERP was charged.
how: FC-R12's text uses the engine's test: ERP charged to the rider and the rider's share of the actual ERP above zero (FC-R06, FC-F04); T53 pins a change with no ERP charged.

claim: CLS-06 reads the reason asymmetrically. Rider reasons match by prefix (startswith 'rider_cancel'), but the no-show reason must equal 'rider_no_show' exactly. 'RIDER_NO_SHOW', 'rider no show' or 'rider_no_show_after_wait' (the suffix style the round 1 cases use for rider reasons) makes a driver no-show case CW-OTHER. Both parties are then told something the record contradicts.
how: Reasons are normalized (case, spaces, hyphens, canceled or cancelled) and read by prefix; RIDER_NO_SHOW and suffixed forms are a no-show reason (V117).

claim: FC-F02's split point 'C on it nearest to where the car was at that moment' is not limited to the part of the route ahead of the car's progress, and it does not say how 'where the car was' is fixed between sparse pings. On a recommended route that passes near itself (an interchange loop, an out-and-back on parallel roads), C can be a point the car passed long before. The distance legitimately driven between that point and the car's real progress then counts as detour.
how: FC-F02 takes C on the part of the route the car had not yet passed, with the car's position at the acceptance interpolated between pings.

claim: When the record says the system canceled but gives no reason, the engine returns REQUEST_INFO and its trace says the driver canceled. CLS-06, the DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition and PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 all send a system cancellation to CW-OTHER. Both parties are told that the record does not settle who canceled, but the record says the system did.
how: As R2-FID-3.

claim: The rules disagree on a driver cancellation that has no reason. CLS-06 and the engine give REQUEST_INFO. The DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition, PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 and D40's summary of CLS-06 send it to CW-OTHER ('another driver ... cancellation', 'another cancellation'). For this branch, explain.py tells both parties the record does not settle who canceled, and GEN-R-NEED-INFO's label says the canceling party cannot be identified. Both are false: the record identifies the driver and only the reason is missing.
how: The DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition and PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 name every CLS-06 branch: a driver cancellation with no reason, records that disagree or cannot be read, or silent records give REQUEST_INFO at tier HUMAN; a system cancellation goes to CW-OTHER. D40's summary of CLS-06 names the branch too (V118).

claim: The safety stand-in still fires on ordinary no-show text. `\baccident` and `\bcrash` match only the start of a word, so they fire on 'accidentally' and 'the app crashed'. `\bunsafe\b` fires on a driver's 'cannot stop here, unsafe', which is the same sentence a4_check pins as must-not-fire with 'dangerous'. The case moves to tier HUMAN, and both parties are told 'The case includes a safety concern'. This contradicts the code comment and D40 (a), which say the patterns match whole words.
how: As R2-FID-5 and ADV2-6; the comment and D40 (a) describe the ignore list.

claim: The EXP-03 verifier's quote exemption (round 1 fix CONS-16) exempts any double-quoted span that appears anywhere inside any rule-card quote. A lone quoted number such as "8", "10" or "$3.00" is therefore exempt, so a made-up number passes the verifier whenever it is put in quotes. EXP-03 exempts only 'a verbatim quote of a clause'.
how: As R2-FID-4.

claim: Round 1 changed stop_added to 'none until the driver accepts' (SG-9, CONS-10), but other text still says the drop-off list changes at stop_added: the dropoffs attribute note, the has_dropoff relation note and D40's summary. The recommended_route note says FC-R12 applies unconditionally, while FC-R12 now applies only when the route could change the amount. D40's summary also still says 'an unsafe drop-off or being stranded', which D40 (f) narrowed.
how: As R2-FID-9 and SG2-8.

claim: itinerary_change treats a destination_edit_requested or stop_added event as a possible change even when its details say the driver declined. FC-R12 then escalates a toll claim the engine would otherwise rule on, although the ontology says a request changes nothing until accepted. FC-R12's ERP materiality wording also differs from the engine at the edges: RydeSEND with ERP charged, and fc_r01 escalating a possible change when the route is marked final_itinerary and no gantry was passed.
how: A request whose details say declined is no change (T48).

claim: The taxonomy was not updated for CLS-06's CW-OTHER branch. CW-DRIVERNOSHOW's excludes still tells a classifier to type any charged fee as CW-RIDERCANCEL or CW-NOSHOW, and CW-OTHER's definition does not say that a fee after a driver cancellation for another reason, or after a system cancellation, belongs there.
how: CW-DRIVERNOSHOW's excludes and CW-OTHER's definition name the CLS-06 branches.

claim: The data contract and evidence lists do not carry the inputs CLS-06 now reads, and no rule or labeling note sets the tier of a REQUEST_INFO outcome, which the engine gives as HUMAN.
how: PB-CW-NOSHOW and PB-CW-RIDERCANCEL list the cancel events and the system message; ENT-TRIP has cancelled_by; CLS-06, the DT precondition and the annotation schema's autonomy_tier note give REQUEST_INFO tier HUMAN.

claim: Some wording still describes the old behavior: PB-CW-RIDERCANCEL step 5 names only one of CW-R08's two FairRyde elements, test V13 still says 'safety language', and the CLS-06 trace prints empty parentheses and cites a field that is absent.
how: PB-CW-RIDERCANCEL step 5 names both FairRyde elements of CW-R08; V13 says 'safety content'; the CLS-06 trace says 'no record names the canceling party' and cites only records that are present.
